symbols.name: Gye Nyame
symbols.meaning: Except God. A symbol of the supremacy and power of God over all things.
symbols.proverb: Except for God, I fear nothing.
symbols.usage: One of the most widely used Adinkra symbols. It appears on walls, fabrics, jewellery, church buildings and business logos across Ghana.

symbols.name: Sankofa
symbols.meaning: Go back and get it. Learn from the past in order to build the future.
symbols.proverb: It is not wrong to go back for that which you have forgotten.
symbols.usage: Often drawn as a bird looking backward or as a heart-like spiral. It is used on cloth, in schools and in memorials to honour history.

symbols.name: Dwennimmen
symbols.meaning: Ram's horns. Strength joined with humility and wisdom.
symbols.proverb: The ram may be strong, yet it still bows its head.
symbols.usage: Chosen for gifts and designs that celebrate quiet strength. It also appears on cloth worn by leaders and elders.

symbols.name: Adinkrahene
symbols.meaning: Chief of the Adinkra symbols. It stands for greatness, charisma and leadership.
symbols.usage: Its concentric circles are said to have inspired the design of several other symbols. It is popular on certificates and ceremonial cloth.

symbols.name: Funtunfunefu Denkyemfunefu
symbols.meaning: Siamese crocodiles. Democracy, unity in diversity and shared destiny.
symbols.proverb: They share one stomach, yet they fight over food.
symbols.usage: Used to remind communities that cooperation matters more than rivalry. It appears in civic buildings and on cloth for community events.

symbols.name: Nyame Dua
symbols.meaning: Tree of God. A sign of God's presence and protection.
symbols.proverb: God's tree stands as an altar of protection.
symbols.usage: Traditionally linked to the altar found in many compounds. It is used to invite blessing and safety into a home.

symbols.name: Aya
symbols.meaning: The fern. Endurance, resourcefulness and the courage to carry on.
symbols.proverb: I am not afraid of you; I have endured hardship.
symbols.usage: Often chosen by people who have come through hard times. It is also found on cloth given to mark perseverance.

symbols.name: Akoma
symbols.meaning: The heart. Patience, tolerance, love and goodwill.
symbols.usage: A common choice for wedding cloth, greeting cards and gifts that express care for another person.

symbols.name: Nkyinkyim
symbols.meaning: Twisting. Initiative, dynamism and the ability to adapt to life's turns.
symbols.proverb: Life's path twists, and the wise person twists with it.
symbols.usage: Used on cloth and artwork that celebrates flexibility and a strong will to keep moving forward.

symbols.name: Duafe
symbols.meaning: The wooden comb. Beauty, care, cleanliness and feminine virtues.
symbols.proverb: A well-kept person shows a well-kept heart.
symbols.usage: Linked to grooming and womanhood. It appears on cloth and gifts for mothers, brides and daughters.

symbols.name: Mate Masie
symbols.meaning: What I hear, I keep. Knowledge, prudence and careful listening.
symbols.usage: Used in settings of counsel and learning. It reminds people to listen well and to guard what they are told.

symbols.name: Ese Ne Tekrema
symbols.meaning: The teeth and the tongue. Friendship and interdependence, with room for disagreement.
symbols.proverb: The teeth and the tongue work together, though sometimes the teeth bite the tongue.
symbols.usage: Offered as a symbol of friendship that survives small quarrels. It is used on gifts between friends and colleagues.

symbols.name: Nea Onnim No Sua A, Ohu
symbols.meaning: He who does not know can know from learning. Lifelong education and the search for knowledge.
symbols.proverb: He who does not know can know from learning.
symbols.usage: Often placed in schools, libraries and graduation materials to celebrate continuous learning.

symbols.name: Bese Saka
symbols.meaning: A bunch of cola nuts. Abundance, trade and the unity of people in commerce.
symbols.proverb: Cola nuts gathered together are a sign of plenty.
symbols.usage: Cola nuts have long been traded and shared as a sign of welcome. The symbol suits markets, cooperatives and business branding.

symbols.name: Boa Me Na Me Mmoa Wo
symbols.meaning: Help me and let me help you. Cooperation and interdependence.
symbols.proverb: Help me, and I will help you.
symbols.usage: Used by groups, associations and teams to express shared effort and mutual support.

symbols.name: Hye Won Hye
symbols.meaning: That which does not burn. Imperishability, endurance and perseverance through hardship.
symbols.usage: Worn to express the ability to withstand trials. It is also used on memorials and in designs about lasting legacy.
